title: Invocation affinity segmentation and hot-path indexing
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: Build a compact, queryable mart that exposes per-tenant and per-route hot-path behaviour by segmenting invocation affinity and indexing dense shards for low-latency ad-hoc queries and dashboards.

Background: Console analytics workloads show a heavy skew: a small fraction of routes and tenants generate very dense invocation patterns and dominate cost and tail latency signals. Current wide-table approaches either bloat storage (full denorm) or produce slow queries when joining sparse identifier sets. This ticket proposes a hybrid design: affinity segmentation to separate 'hot' invocation streams into shard tables with histogram-backed indexes and a sparse canonical layer for long-tail joins.

Goals:
- Provide sub-second dashboard slices for top 500 tenant-route combinations over 30d windows.
- Maintain a compact canonical invocation layer for ad-hoc cross-tenant joins.
- Reduce query CPU by ~40% for hot-path queries through shard pruning + pre-aggregated histograms.
- Provide an operational eviction policy for hot shards and an automated backfill strategy.

Scope: design and implement the data model, ETL transforms (beam/spark), MV refresh schedule, and dashboard queries. Out of scope: UI redesign and long-term cold storage compaction (separate follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Schema proposal reviewed and approved by data platform and console backend teams
ETL pipeline produces hot-shard tables and canonical invocation table on staging with sampling parity to prod (samples within 0.5% of baseline)
Top-500 tenant-route dashboard queries return in <1.2s P95 on staging cluster sizes equivalent to prod
Automated shard eviction marks low-traffic shards for compaction and triggers backfill within SLA
PRs for transformations merged and release notes added to console-2026.04
comments: 2026-02-06 - Spike: ingested 48 hours of invocation events into local dev cluster; observed 87% of tokens come from top 3% of route-tenant keys. Sketches and histograms reduce raw row counts by ~6x for hot shards.

2026-02-18 - Design review: decided on tenant-route as primary shard key plus time-bucket (H3-like day-bucket) rather than model-variant to keep joins cheap for per-route dashboards. PM requested include model_variant_id as a dimension in histograms.
2026-02-25 - Engineering note: prototype uses t-digest for quantiles and Count-Min for heavy hitters; switched from hyperloglog due to cardinality constraints on ephemeral attributes.
2026-03-02 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls/2149 - ETL job writing hot_shard_{date} and canonical_invocation_v1. Pending data platform review for partitioning strategy.

2026-03-08 - Review feedback from Data Platform: prefer integer shard_id computed via consistent hashing + tenant fingerprint for stable shard assignment. Also suggested SST-based compaction windows for cold shards.
2026-03-10 - Infra: scheduled staging run for nightly backfill; observed initial runtime 2.6h, optimizing vectorized writes next week. Assigned Marcus to follow up on write amplification.
Next steps: finalize shard eviction thresholds, add alerting for hot-shard overflow, and create runbook for emergency compaction during tenant spikes.
implementation_notes:
Data model:
- hot_shards (partitioned by shard_id, date) columns: shard_id, day_bucket, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant_id, invocation_count, token_count, tdigest_quantiles_base64, cms_heavy_hitters_base64, last_updated_ts.
- canonical_invocations (append-only) columns: event_id, ts, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant_id, token_count, metadata_fingerprint

Shard assignment: stable consistent hash(tenant_id || route_id) -> N shards per day; dynamic N depends on observed density (auto-scale signal).

Aggregation windows: hourly ingestion producing day-bucketed histograms and sketches. Use t-digest with 200 centroids and CMS with width 2^16 for heavy hitters. Store binary blobs base64-encoded to keep schema simple.

Eviction & Backfill: define TTL_soft and TTL_hard per shard density percentile. Eviction marks a shard for compaction into canonical_invocations and registers a backfill job that can be retried. Backfill uses time-windowed micro-batches to avoid large spikes.

Query patterns and MVs: create pre-aggregated materialized views for top-k tenants per org and histogram_cubes for rapid percentile lookups. Use partition pruning on shard_id + day_bucket to keep queries under SLA.

Operational: alert when hot_shard write latency > 2s or when shard size > 500GB un-compacted. Backfill SLA: start within 1 hour and complete within 12 hours for shards < 7 days old.

Backfill plan: incremental replay from raw event lake using watermark offsets; backfill jobs are idempotent by watermark checkpointing. Performance tuning: vectorized parquet writes, batching by shard_id, and asynchronous uploads to iceberg partitions.
